messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- On 2026-06-09 the Dune team observed that the indexer's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change. [valid 2026-06-09 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2026-06-09]
- On 2026-05-27 the Atlas team noticed that the indexer's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-05-27 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-05-27]
- On 2026-04-01, ownership of the indexer transferred from the Atlas team to the Boreal team. [valid 2026-04-01 to now; recorded by handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer]
- The indexer was owned by the Atlas team from 2025-05-20, taking over from Cinder, until ownership transferred to the Boreal team on 2026-04-01. [decision; valid 2026-04-01 to now; recorded by handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer]
    earlier: The indexer is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-05-20, taking over from Cinder. [decision; valid 2025-05-20 to 2026-04-01; recorded by handover/2025-05-20-search-indexer]
    earlier: The indexer is owned by Cinder. [valid 2025-01-17 to 2025-05-20; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-01-17-2]
- As of 2026-04-01, the pager for the indexer rings the Boreal team, not the Atlas team. [valid 2026-04-01 to now; recorded by handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer]
- On 2026-02-10 the Boreal team noticed that the indexer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-02-10 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-02-10-2]
- On 2026-04-16 the Atlas team noticed that the ledger service's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-16 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-16]
- On 2025-12-18 the Atlas team decided that the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every product catalog write, because incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes. [decision; valid 2025-12-18 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-12-18]
- On 2026-06-04 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-06-04 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-06-04]
- The indexer relies on the product catalog for product documents, so if the product catalog is down the indexer is down. [valid 2025-01-30 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-01-30]
- On 2026-04-08 the Atlas team noticed that webhooks' request volume halved following the client rollout and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-08 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-08]
- The indexer is pinned to OpenSearch 2.11 until the full reindex completes. [constraint; valid 2025-04-22 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-22]
- On 2026-03-20 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change. [valid 2026-03-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-03-20-2]
- In INC-2025-023, the indexer served stale results for two days starting 2025-10-03 because a reindex job failed silently on a full disk. [valid 2025-10-07 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-023]
- On 2025-12-25 the Atlas team noticed that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2025-12-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-12-25]
- As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Atlas team, having moved from the Ember team; the Dune team never owned it. [decision; valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction]
    earlier: As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Dune team, having moved from the Ember team. [decision; valid 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-09; recorded by handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags]
- The feature-flags service was owned by the Ember team as of 2025-11-06, having moved from the Atlas team, until ownership transferred to the Atlas team on 2026-02-11. [decision; valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction]
    earlier: The feature-flags service was owned by the Ember team as of 2025-11-06, having moved from the Atlas team, until ownership transferred to the Dune team on 2026-02-11. [decision; valid 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-09; recorded by handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags]
    earlier: As of 2025-11-06, the feature-flags service is owned by the Ember team, having moved from the Atlas team. [decision; valid 2025-11-06 to 2026-02-11; recorded by handover/2025-11-06-feature-flags]

Question: Which team owns the service that search-indexer depends on?

But the 2026-06-04 entry says "pinged the owners" which suggests Boreal is not the owner.

Hmm, this is tricky. The pattern in this memory set: when a team notices an issue on a service they don't own, the entry says "and flagged it because it is not their service" or "and pinged the owners". The 2026-03-20 entry has neither, suggesting Boreal owns the product catalog. But 2026-06-04 says "pinged the owners" for product catalog, contradicting.

Wait, let me re-read: "On 2026-06-04 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners." Yes, pinged the owners.

"On 2026-03-20 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change." No ping/flag.

Hmm. These are contradictory inferences. Without explicit ownership info, the safest answer per the rules is "I don't know". But maybe the intended answer is Boreal based on the 2026-03-20 entry pattern (absence of "not their service" disclaimer). Actually, in these synthetic memory tests, the pattern is: entries with "flagged it because it is not their service" indicate non-owners; entries without it indicate the noticing team owns the service. The 2026-03-20 entry lacks the disclaimer → Boreal owns product catalog. The 2026-06-04 entry has "pinged the owners" — hmm, but that could also be interpreted as... no, "pinged the owners" clearly means someone else owns it.

Hmm wait, maybe "pinged the owners" could be a team pinging... no. Let me think about which is more reliable. Actually, maybe the test intends: the question is a multi-hop: indexer depends on product catalog; product catalog owned by Boreal (inferred from 2026-03-20 entry lacking the disclaimer). The 2026-06-04 entry might be a distractor or might indicate... hmm.

Actually, let me reconsider. Perhaps the intended reading: "pinged the owners" entries are all cases where the noticing team is not the owner:
- 2026-05-27 Atlas on indexer (owner Boreal) ✓
- 2026-02-10 Boreal on indexer (owner Atlas) ✓
- 2026-06-04 Boreal on product catalog → Boreal not owner?

And "flagged it because it is not their service":
- 2026-04-16 Atlas on ledger ✓ not owner
- 2026-04-08 Atlas on webhooks ✓ not owner
- 2025-12-25 Atlas on reports pipeline ✓ not owner

And no disclaimer:
- 2026-06-09 Dune on indexer disk usage — indexer owner is Boreal. Hmm! Dune noticed indexer disk usage jump with no disclaimer. That breaks the pattern if absence of disclaimer implies ownership. So absence of disclaimer doesn't imply ownership.
- 2026-03-20 Boreal on product catalog — no disclaimer.

So the pattern isn't reliable. Dune noticed indexer issue without disclaimer, but Dune doesn't own the indexer (Boreal does). So absence of disclaimer means nothing.

Therefore, there's no explicit ownership statement for the product catalog in memory. The answer should be "I don't know".

Hmm, but wait — could the question be interpreted differently? "the service that search-indexer depends on" — the indexer relies on the product catalog. Ownership of product catalog: not stated. So "I don't know".

But maybe the intended answer is Boreal via the 2026-03-20 entry. Given the Dune/indexer counterexample, the absence-of-disclaimer inference is invalid. The rules say don't guess. So "I don't know".

Actually, let me double check: is there any entry stating product catalog ownership? Scanning... No. Only observations by Boreal. No handover entries for product catalog.

So answer: I don't know.
